transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Pegasus Head of Security), Priya Raman (VP Engineering), Liam O'Neill (SRE)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
- Rapid security posture discovery, focus on hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs for regulated finance workloads.
- Key controls: SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency/retention.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Park: ok hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on your account, with me is Maya our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Ethan Cole: thanks Jordan, Ethan here; quick note we have Priya and Liam on as well, we wanted to run through your security posture as part of vendor risk and figure out fit.
[00:13] Priya Raman: hi all, busy week so appreciate the run through.
[00:17] Maya Singh: cool, we'll try to keep it tight. quick agenda: SOC2/ISO status, auth (SSO/SAML), RBAC model, audit logs & retention, encryption and KMS integration, deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), and then next steps. sound good?
[00:29] Liam O'Neill: yep sounds great.
[00:31] Jordan Park: quick housekeeping, i'll capture action items, and we'll share our SOC2 and iso artifacts redacted of course.

[00:40] Ethan Cole: first question, are you SOC2 type II and do you have ISO 27001 evidence? we need the reports for our vendor review.
[00:48] Maya Singh: yes we maintain SOC 2 Type II, we completed the last audit in Q4 2026, we also have an ISO 27001 certification in place for our control plane; we'll send the certificate and the SOC2 report - redacted where necessary - as part of the packet.
[00:59] Ethan Cole: ok, and do you host customer data in shared infrastructure for hosted offering?
[01:04] Jordan Park: for hosted API it's multi-tenant at the control plane level but customer data is logically separated and we offer strong encryption at rest, also retention controls. for higher isolation we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem) which give you network isolation and customer-managed keys.
[01:23] Priya Raman: could you explain the KMS flow for the dedicated/private options? does Redwood ever see plaintext keys or data?
[01:30] Maya Singh: good question. in Private, customers can bring-your-own-key via cloud KMS or HSM - Redwood doesn't have access to the KMS key material; we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a set of HSM integrations. in Dedicated we offer optional KMS integration so keys can be customer-managed; again we don't store raw key material. for hosted by default it's Redwood-managed keys but we can discuss CMEK for enterprise agreements.
[01:52] Ethan Cole: so with Dedicated we can ensure keys are customer-managed, that's important. what about encryption in transit and the ciphers used?
[01:58] Maya Singh: TLS1.2+ with recommended cipher suites; mutual TLS is available for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we support mTLS for certain enterprise plans.

[02:12] Liam O'Neill: audit logs - how granular are they? we need per-request logs including model called, request id, timestamps, and operator identity.
[02:20] Maya Singh: audit logs include request metadata, model and route, tokens processed, timestamps, and the principal identity when available; we can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging endpoints, or provide buckets with logs exported on a schedule. note sometimes the transcript text may be redacted for PII depending on retention policy.
[02:40] Ethan Cole: retention, what's the default and can we set retention policy to 90/180/365 days?
[02:46] Jordan Park: default is 30 days on hosted for generated content, but we support configurable retention windows for Dedicated/Private; we can do 90/180/365 based on plan and storage. for compliance we can also do long-term archive to your own S3 with lifecycle rules.
[03:01] Priya Raman: what about RBAC and least privilege? we need fine-grained roles for dev, infra, security, and app teams.
[03:09] Maya Singh: Redwood supports RBAC with built-in roles and custom roles. you can gate actions like model deployment, rollout, viewing logs, and billing. SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported for provisioning and role mapping so you can map IDP groups to roles.
[03:24] Ethan Cole: do you support SCIM for automated user de-provisioning?
[03:27] Maya Singh: yes we do SCIM for user lifecycle, and SAML 2.0 for SSO. small note sometimes our older docs show OIDC examples - but SAML + SCIM are the primary enterprise flow.

[03:44] Jordan Park: on the private deployment, network wise we offer two patterns: 1) VPC peering/endpoint where control plane is still run by Redwood but data plane is customer-hosted; 2) fully private on-prem package where both control and data plane are customer-run, for the most regulated use cases.
[03:59] Liam O'Neill: if we go VPC peering, what's the egress pattern? do connections originate from our VPC to Redwood or vice versa? we need to manage firewall rules.
[04:08] Maya Singh: typically for VPC endpoint the traffic originates from your VPC to our endpoints over TLS, we provide exact IP ranges and additional routing guidance; if you need inbound connections we can discuss ingress via secure tunnels but most customers prefer outbound. we'll share the network diagram.

[04:26] Ethan Cole: about logging - do you provide immutable audit trails? we need tamper evidence for certain logs.
[04:33] Maya Singh: we support append-only logs with retention and can sign logs for tamper evidence, plus we can stream to customer-managed S3 or SIEM which helps. for Dedicated/Private we can also integrate with customer WORM storage for regulatory requirements.

[04:50] Priya Raman: service uptime SLAs? for dedicated we'd want a 99.9% SLA and documented incident response and runbooks.
[04:57] Jordan Park: Dedicated includes SLA options and runbook access; incident response times vary by support tier, we can provide our NOC and escalation matrix. we'll include the SLA document in the follow up.

[05:07] Liam O'Neill: there will be a security questionnaire from procurement with 200+ controls; do you have a standard answers pack or a security pack we can attach?
[05:15] Jordan Park: yes we maintain a vendor security pack - SOC2 report, pen test summary, encryption matrix, network diagrams - we'll send that. also we have a maturity matrix we can fill out.

[05:24] Ethan Cole: curious about data residency - our customers are EU-based, can you guarantee data residency in eu regions for hosted?
[05:31] Maya Singh: we have EU regions and can route and store EU customer data in region; for regulatory needs some customers prefer Dedicated in a region or Private deployment.

[05:40] Priya Raman: one ask: for PoC we'd want to run latency and throughput benchmarks using our prompts and model footprint, and we'd like a cost model for dedicated vs hosted.
[05:48] Jordan Park: absolutely, for PoC we'll coordinate benchmark scripts, provide model variants and quantization options, and give a cost estimate. Maya will lead the perf scoping.

[05:59] Maya Singh: quick note on model variants - for perf we may suggest quantized variants and batching configs; we'll capture expected token lengths and we'll run with your sample workload. also mention caching/prefix cache options to reduce cost.

[06:15] Ethan Cole: any major third-party sub processors we should be aware of? e.g., cloud providers, observability vendors?
[06:20] Jordan Park: primary sub-processors are AWS, GCP, Azure depending on region, plus observability tooling like Datadog for our hosted control plane; all are listed in our data processing addendum.

[06:31] Liam O'Neill: last technical question - how do you handle KV cache and possible PII leakage from cached prefixes?
[06:38] Maya Singh: KV cache is tenant-isolated; we have policies to scrub known PII and options to disable caching per-route. for regulated data you can disable cache or use private deployments where cache lives in your VPC.

[06:54] Jordan Park: great, i think that's the primary coverage - want to recap next steps?
[06:58] Ethan Cole: yes please.

Recap / Next steps:
[07:03] Jordan Park: we'll send SOC2 Type II, ISO cert, security pack, and SLA doc (owner: Jordan, due 2027-02-10).
[07:10] Maya Singh: i'll share VPC diagram, KMS integration notes, audit log schema, and a perf scoping sheet (owner: Maya, due 2027-02-12).
[07:17] Ethan Cole: we'll fill out the security questionnaire and propose PoC dates (owner: Pegasus, due 2027-02-15).
[07:22] Priya Raman: we'll confirm team availability for the perf window week of 2027-02-22.

[07:28] Jordan Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the artifact pack and schedule.
[07:32] Priya Raman: thanks, bye.
[07:34] (call ends)

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings; product names may appear slightly different in transcript. references shared: link to security pack (redwood.com/security-pack), VPC diagram (link will be shared), SOC2 report (attached in follow-up).
